extracted.intended_audience: parties and practitioners in PTAB proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, patent practitioners), and Board judges/administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing, serving, and litigating petitions and motions in PTAB proceedings (post‑grant review, covered business method review, derivation), and limits on Board/Office involvement in panel decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content — identification of claims and relief requested
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must request judgment against one or more identified patent claims and set forth the precise relief requested for each challenged claim, including identification of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to other required notices (e.g., §§ 42.6, 42.8, 42.22, 42.24), the petition must clearly identify which claim(s) are challenged and the precise relief sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content — statutory grounds identified
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must identify the specific statutory grounds (e.g., those permitted under 35 U.S.C. 282(b) as modified) on which each challenged claim is attacked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For covered business method and post‑grant petitions, the petition must state which statutory grounds support the challenge (if alleging unpatentability other than by prior art, identify the statutory provision and explain the failure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content — claim construction requirement (means/step‑plus‑function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claim contains a means‑plus‑function or step‑plus‑function limitation under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the petition must identify the specific portions of the specification that describe the structure, material, or acts corresponding to each claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pinpoint the spec language supporting the claimed function(s); this applies in petitions (post‑grant, CBM, derivation) and to proposed substitute claims in motions to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content — showing how construed claim is unpatentable
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must explain how the construed claim is unpatentable under the statutory grounds identified; if based on prior art, specify where each element of the claim is found in the prior art; for other grounds identify the specific part of the claim that fails and explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must provide element‑by‑element mappings to prior art when applicable and specific statutory noncompliance explanations for non‑prior art grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content — exhibits and pinpointing evidence relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must state the exhibit numbers of supporting evidence and the relevance of the evidence to the challenge, including identifying specific portions of the evidence that support the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may exclude or give no weight to evidence where a party fails to state its relevance or to identify specific portions that support the challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of petition — address and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must serve the petition and exhibits on the patent owner at the correspondence address of record; may also serve other addresses likely to effect service. Parties may agree to electronic service. Service may be by Priority Mail Express® or means at least as fast and reliable; personal service not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow § 42.6 requirements as well; ensure service on the correspondence address of record to effect filing and institution rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date — completeness conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition will not be accorded a filing date until it: (1) complies with the applicable content rules (e.g., § 42.204 or § 42.304), (2) effects service as required, and (3) is accompanied by the required filing fee (§ 42.15(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three elements must be satisfied for a filing date to be accorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date — incomplete petition cure period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party files an incomplete petition, no filing date is accorded and the Office will dismiss the request if the deficiency is not corrected within the earlier of one month from notice of incompleteness or the expiration of the statutory deadline to file the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely correction is mandatory to avoid dismissal; clerical/typographical correction motions do not change the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary response — scope and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a preliminary response limited to setting forth reasons why no post‑grant review should be instituted under 35 U.S.C. 324; it may include supporting evidence but shall not include any amendment. The preliminary response is subject to the word count under § 42.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the preliminary response can be waived (expedited) by the patent owner by filing an election to waive the preliminary response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary response — due date
rubrics_metrics.description: The preliminary response must be filed no later than three months after the date of a notice indicating the petition has been accorded a filing date. A patent owner may expedite the proceeding by waiving the preliminary response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the three‑month deadline unless a Board order provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimers of claims prior to institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a statutory disclaimer under 35 U.S.C. 253(a) disclaiming one or more claims; no post‑grant review will be instituted based on disclaimed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclaimer can remove claims from institution considerations but must comply with § 1.321(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard — 'more likely than not' threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Post‑grant review shall not be instituted unless the Board decides the information presented in the petition demonstrates it is more likely than not that at least one challenged claim is unpatentable. The Board's decision will take into account a patent owner preliminary response, including any testimonial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the institution threshold; petitions must meet the preponderance‑likelihood showing to proceed. Petitioner may seek leave to reply to the preliminary response for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution consideration of novel legal questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient grounds for institution may include a showing that the petition raises a novel or unsettled legal question important to other patents or patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legal‑question basis can support institution even where factual showings vary, if the issue has broader importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response after institution — scope and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: After institution, a patent owner may file a single response to the petition and/or decision on institution as an opposition; the response is subject to the page limits provided in § 42.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board does not provide a filing date for the owner response, the default due date is three months from institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — timing and conferral requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may file one original motion to amend, but only after conferring with the Board. Unless a due date is provided in a Board order, the original motion must be filed no later than the filing of the patent owner response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preliminary guidance is desired, the request must be included in the original motion to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — permissible scope and denials
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend may be denied where: (i) the amendment does not respond to a ground of unpatentability involved in the trial; or (ii) the amendment seeks to enlarge the scope of the claims or introduce new subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions that expand scope or add new matter are improper; amendments should be responsive to trial issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — reasonable number of substitute claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend may cancel a challenged claim or propose a reasonable number of substitute claims. The presumption is that only one substitute claim will be needed to replace each challenged claim, which may be rebutted by a demonstration of need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board presumes one substitute per challenged claim unless justified otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend — required content/support
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend must include a claim listing (may be in an appendix), show changes clearly, and set forth: (1) the support in the original disclosure of the patent for each proposed substitute claim; and (2) the support in an earlier‑filed disclosure for each claim for which benefit of the earlier filing date is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must provide clear support citations to the original disclosure and any earlier disclosures relied upon for priority benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional motion to amend — Board authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, any additional motion to amend may not be filed without Board authorization. An additional motion may be authorized for good cause or where jointly requested to materially advance a settlement. The Board will consider whether a petitioner submitted supplemental information after the motion period when deciding authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek Board authorization and demonstrate good cause or settlement advancement to file additional motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of persuasion on motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: On any motion to amend: (1) the patent owner bears the burden to show by a preponderance of the evidence that the motion complies with statutory requirements and section requirements; (2) the petitioner bears the burden to show by a preponderance that any proposed substitute claims are unpatentable; and (3) the Board may exercise discretion to grant or deny a motion or to raise a new ground of unpatentability in connection with a proposed substitute claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both sides carry preponderance burdens; Board discretion may introduce new grounds with notice and opportunity to respond; determinations are on the preponderance of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board consideration of additional evidence and examination assistance on motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may consider all evidence of record and may make of record evidence from related proceedings, district courts (judicially noticed), and information identified in response to Board‑initiated examination assistance. The Board may request examination assistance when appropriate and will make the results of such assistance of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board has broad latitude to consider related records and to request exam assistance if prior art challenges warrant additional search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary guidance on motion to amend — nonbinding and procedural effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may request preliminary guidance on its original motion to amend; the Board may provide initial views on whether parties have shown a reasonable likelihood of meeting their burdens and may notify of any new ground discretionary raised. Preliminary guidance is not binding, is not a 'decision' subject to rehearing or Director Review, and is not final agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies and sur‑replies to preliminary guidance have strict limits: replies may include new evidence; sur‑replies generally may not; petitioner replies to preliminary guidance may not include new evidence; sequencing and permissible content are tightly controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised motion to amend — one post‑opportunity filing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Irrespective of the additional‑motion rule, a patent owner may file one revised motion to amend without prior authorization after receiving an opposition to the original motion or after receiving the Board's preliminary guidance. The revised motion must be responsive to issues raised and include one or more new proposed substitute claims; a revised motion replaces the original motion in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised motion must present new claim amendments responsive to the opposition or preliminary guidance; filing may prompt Board to request schedule extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple proceedings and joinder timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where another matter involving the patent is before the Office, the Board may enter orders regarding stay, transfer, consolidation, or termination of that matter. Joinder may be requested by patent owner or petitioner as a motion under § 42.22 no later than one month after the institution date of any post‑grant review for which joinder is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File joinder requests within one month of the relevant institution date; the Board has broad case‑management authority across related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information — timing and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a trial is instituted, a party may file a motion to submit supplemental information within one month of institution; the supplemental information must be relevant to a claim for which the trial has been instituted. Late submissions (more than one month after institution) require authorization and must show why the supplemental information reasonably could not have been obtained earlier and that consideration would be in the interests of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental filings are tightly time‑bounded and must be justified if late; unrelated supplemental information requires separate authorization and similar showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery limits — good cause and direct relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for additional discovery may be granted upon a showing of good cause why the discovery is needed, and discovery is limited to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by either party in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is narrower than in district court — must tie requests to specific factual assertions and show good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered Business Method (CBM) review — applicability and pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: A CBM patent review is a trial under subpart A and is subject to post‑grant review procedures except for specific sections; claim construction uses the same standard as in a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 282(b) (ordinary and customary meaning as understood by one of ordinary skill and prosecution history). Pendency after institution is normally no more than one year, with possible extension up to six months for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM petitions are available only for patents claiming data processing or operations used in financial products/services (excluding technological inventions); prior claim constructions from civil actions or ITC that are timely made of record will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBM — definition of technological invention
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether a patent is for a technological invention (and thus excluded from CBM), consider whether the claimed subject matter as a whole recites a technological feature that is novel and unobvious over the prior art and solves a technical problem using a technical solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess technological features and technical problem/solution; CBM excludes patents for technological inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBM petition — standing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may not file a CBM petition unless the petitioner (or real party‑in‑interest or privy) has been sued for infringement or charged with infringement — i.e., there is a real and substantial controversy such that the petitioner would have standing in Federal court; estoppel rules also bar certain petitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate CBM status of the patent and the petitioner's eligibility under § 42.302 in the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation petition — who may file and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for patent may file a petition for a derivation proceeding. The petition must be filed within one year beginning on the date of first publication of a claim to an invention that is the same or substantially the same as the earlier application's claim alleged to have been derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the one‑year publication trigger and ensure petitioner status (applicant) before filing; include the required derivation fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation petition — fee and filing date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A derivation fee (§ 42.15(c)) must accompany the petition and no filing date will be accorded until payment is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is required to obtain a filing date; incomplete filings without payment will be dismissed if not corrected within the cure period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation petition — content and sufficiency of showing
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must demonstrate compliance with filing/timing rules and show the petitioner has at least one claim that is (i) the same or substantially the same as the respondent’s claimed invention and (ii) the same or substantially the same as the invention disclosed to the respondent. The petition must show the claimed invention was derived from an inventor named in the petitioner’s application and that the inventor did not authorize the filing of the earlier application. A derivation showing is not sufficient unless supported by substantial evidence, including at least one affidavit addressing communication and lack of authorization that is corroborated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient corroborated evidence (including at least one affidavit) demonstrating communication of the derived invention and lack of authorization to file the earlier application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation — claim construction requirement (means/step‑plus‑function)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each of the respondent’s claims to the derived invention, the petition must identify how the claim is to be construed; for means/step‑plus‑function limitations under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), identify the specific portions of the specification that describe the structure, material, or acts corresponding to each claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same pinpointing requirement as in other petition contexts — identify supporting spec passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration — conditions for Board recognition and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may resort to binding arbitration (Office not party; Board not bound). The Board will not set or modify proceedings for arbitration unless (inter alia) the arbitration is under Title 9, parties notify the Board, the agreement is in writing, specifies issues, names arbitrator or sets a selection date, provides that the award is binding and judgment may be entered by the Board, a copy is filed within 20 days, and arbitration is completed within Board‑set time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are solely responsible for arbitrator selection and conduct; Board may determine issues arbitration does not resolve and will not consider an arbitration award unless it is binding, in writing, states each issue and disposition, and is filed within 20 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of Board records and publication discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Board decisions are available for public inspection if rendered in a file open to the public or in a published application; the Office may independently publish any Board decision available for public inspection. A Board decision not otherwise publishable may be published if the Director finds special circumstances and a party does not object within two months on confidentiality/trade secret grounds with specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must timely object with specific claims of confidential trade secrets to prevent publication; otherwise decisions in public files may be made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Director and senior officials’ pre‑issuance involvement in panel decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to issuance of a panel decision, the Director, Deputy Director, Commissioner for Patents, and Commissioner for Trademarks shall not communicate, directly or through intermediaries, with any panel member regarding the decision. This prohibition does not apply if one of those individuals is a member of the panel (they then act as a coequal panel member). Communications about resource needs or procedural status are permitted. The Chief Administrative Patent Judge (or delegates) shall designate panels only in accordance with public Board paneling guidance; the Director may issue generally applicable paneling guidance but shall not direct paneling or repaneling of any specific proceeding prior to issuance of the panel decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain institutional and decisional independence of panels; Director may only repanel via Order when reviewing or rehearing consistent with public guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision definition and management judge roles
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Decision' means any decision, order, opinion, or other written work product intended for entry into the record of a Board proceeding. 'Management Judge' includes specified leadership positions (Chief Administrative Patent Judge, Deputy, Vice Chief, Senior Lead, Lead APJ) including acting incumbents and other APJs who serve as rating officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions clarify terminology used in limits on involvement and decision circulation rules.
